title: Machine-learning Immune Profile Score stratifies survival on checkpoint inhibitors
summary: The Immune Profile Score was developed in 1,707 patients and validated in 1,600 patients with advanced solid cancers across 16 types treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors in a real-world database. IPS-High patients had longer overall survival than IPS-Low (HR 0.45, 90% CI 0.40 to 0.52), and the score remained significant after controlling for TMB, MSI and PD-L1. The data are retrospective and the score is mainly prognostic; predictive utility was exploratory.
ai_technology: Machine learning framework combining tumor mutational burden and 11 RNA-based biomarkers from Tempus xT/xR sequencing to build the Immune Profile Score

evidence.tested: Retrospective validation in a separate cohort of 1,600 patients; HR 0.45 for overall survival.
evidence.unknown: Prospective utility and treatment-selection value; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine learning model combining TMB and RNA biomarkers into a survival-stratifying score

source_review.scope: Abstract read from Europe PMC metadata for this DOI; author affiliations from the same record. Publisher full text not accessed.
